extracted.intended_audience: small businesses seeking NIAID SBIR/STTR funding (applicants and applicant organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Step‑by‑step guidance for small business concerns to determine eligibility, register, select appropriate NIAID SBIR/STTR funding opportunities, prepare and submit an application, and manage post-submission and award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting an application, determine whether your small business concern qualifies for NIAID’s Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NIH’s Small Business Eligibility Criteria for more information; confirm small business concern status, ownership, size, and other eligibility rules before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Required Registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Small businesses must complete several required registrations before submitting an application to NIH; a process which can take 6 to 8 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete registrations as described on the NIH SEED Required Company Registrations page and ensure your business has a valid Employer Identification Number. Use NIH Grants & Funding Organization Registrations resources and Preparing to Apply podcasts for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Funding Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the Funding Mechanisms section for an outline of the differences between grants, contracts, and cooperative agreements in the SBIR/STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the mechanism that fits your project goals (e.g., grant vs contract vs cooperative agreement) since mechanism affects application requirements and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose Topic and Ensure Alignment with NIAID Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore High‑Priority Areas of Interest for the NIAID Small Business Program to determine if your topic is prioritized for program acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NIAID Program Descriptions and Research Topics document, SBIR and STTR Omnibus Grant Solicitations, and recent SBIR Contract solicitations. Topics that align with NIAID priorities may be encouraged or have different submission pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult NIAID Small Business Program Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with a member of the NIAID Small Business Program Team for feedback regarding the scope and commercialization objectives for your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this consultation to connect with scientific program staff and get program‑level feedback prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH RePORTER and Matchmaker to Survey the Field
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse the NIH RePORTER research portfolio database and use the Matchmaker tool to find information on current projects approved for NIH funding, awarded project amounts, and competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning what has been funded, award sizes, and potential competitors helps refine your proposal and commercialization plan. See 'Find Funded Projects and More Using NIH Databases.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Appropriate Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
rubrics_metrics.description: After carrying out the preparatory steps, select a funding opportunity. Refer to the NIH SBIR/STTR Funding page for opportunity overview information and find a complete list of NIAID participating NOFOs at Funding Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the NOFO you select matches your project stage and goals and note any institute‑specific participation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the Full NOFO and SBIR/STTR Application Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to read the full NOFO for detailed instructions before beginning your application. Download the SBIR/STTR Application Instructions to use as a reference during the grant application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NOFO‑specific instructions exactly; sections of the NOFO (and the SBIR/STTR instructions) may contain mandatory formatting, content, or submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Application Preparation Guidance and Use Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Find guidance on writing a strong application at NIAID’s Apply for a Grant and NIH’s Prepare Your Application. For examples of successful applications, refer to R41, R42, R43, and R44 Small Business - Sample Applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample applications and summary statements as references when preparing your submission. Review example forms, data sharing and model organism sharing plans, biographical sketches, and other supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe NIAID Budget Caps and Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications exceeding NIAID budget caps may be withdrawn from funding consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the 'Budget: Hard Caps, Small Business Administration (SBA) Waiver, and NIAID Budget Request Limitations' section of the Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer Grants SOP for current caps and waiver processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow SBIR/STTR‑Specific Application Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay close attention to SBIR/STTR Application Instruction items marked 'Additional Instructions for SBIR/STTR.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special programs (e.g., Commercialization Readiness Pilot (CRP)) may modify standard instructions—CRP applicants should note Section IV of the CRP NOFO contains extensive changes/additions to the standard instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit Electronically Using NIH Submission Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Your organization must submit SBIR and STTR grant applications electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH’s ASSIST (Application Submission System and Interface for Submission Tracking) or one of the other NIH Submission Options. Refer to NIH's 'How to Submit, Track, and View Your Application' for step‑by‑step submission and tracking guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for Post‑Submission Review and Just‑in‑Time Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, learn the next steps including the Review Process, Scoring & Summary Statements, and contacting your program officer for advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'After You Submit an Application' for details. Be prepared to respond to pre‑award requests ('Just‑in‑Time') if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Award and Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If awarded, follow guidance in 'Manage Your Award' which covers reporting requirements and other post‑award responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand ongoing obligations including financial and progress reporting, compliance, and award management expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Eligibility After Organizational Legal Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a legal action (e.g., merger, acquisition, or successor‑in‑interest) changes your organization status so that it is no longer eligible for SBIR/STTR programs, existing awards cannot receive additional funds and the organization would not be eligible for new SBIR/STTR grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the NIH awarding office in advance of legal actions that may affect organizational eligibility. Refer to NIH Grants Policy Statement, Section 8.1.2.8 'Change in Recipient Organizational Status.' NIH will negotiate bilateral terminations when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH and NIAID Applicant Support Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage NIH SBIR/STTR program resources like Product Development Support, I‑Corps at NIH, the SBIR/STTR Commercialization Readiness Pilot (CRP), and Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs provide commercialization training, technical and business assistance, and other supports (e.g., TABA Needs Assessment). First‑time applicants are encouraged to review these resources prior to submitting an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference NIAID Small Business Program Pages for Additional Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the main NIAID Small Business Programs page for funding opportunities, high‑priority areas of research interest, success stories, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institute pages to stay current on priorities, opportunities, and example projects; these help tailor applications to NIAID interests.
